minutes.headline: Board withholds releasing a tax lien on a Chapter Land property until the owner pays years of back taxes owed.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors reviewed routine business — prior minutes, excise tax abatement procedure, pending vision/commercial valuations, and new-growth estimates — then spent most of the meeting on a long-running dispute over a Chapter Land (CL9) property where the owner underpaid taxes for years; the board decided to keep the lien in place until back taxes are paid. It also discussed GIS/mapping software costs, an update to the veterans' property tax exemption for the November special town meeting, a staffing departure, and senior means-tested exemption applications, before adjourning into executive session.

budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor reported the number and total dollar value of excise tax abatements processed in August via the automatic-sign process; the board agreed to formally review them at the next meeting.
The board discussed a preliminary new-growth/assessed-value figure so far this year, noting it looked lower than the prior year or two but that commercial figures were still outstanding.

budget_items.topic: Chapter Land (CL9) back taxes owed, Sunny Hill Road property
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff presented a supporting spreadsheet showing the total back taxes owed by the property owner as of a stated date, with interest continuing to accrue until paid.
A board member noted that a GIS vendor would likely charge a per-layer fee if the town wanted custom visualization layers built for the neighborhood project.
A board member relayed new ArcGIS Online pricing tiers under consideration for the neighborhood/mapping project, from a basic to a professional tier.
A board member recalled the town had budgeted a smaller amount previously for mapping services through CI and thought there was room in that budget to cover new costs.

The board discussed that the veterans exemption has been at a minimum amount for a long time and considered proposing an increase, noting any increase is funded entirely by the town with no reimbursement.

budget_items.topic: Senior means-tested exemption program, budget and applications
budget_items.what_was_said: The board reviewed how many households applied for and received the senior means-tested tax exemption, comparing it to the prior year, and confirmed the amount set aside was sufficient.

decisions.decision: The 49 excise tax abatements from August, already stamped, will be formally reviewed and added to the next meeting's agenda rather than reviewed tonight.
The town will forego pursuing rollback taxes on the Chapter Land property and instead collect only the currently owed back taxes on what is now three or four separate parcels.
The board will not release or sign off on the Chapter Land (CL9) lien releases until the town actually receives the back tax payment from the property owner.
A placeholder will be requested for a veterans' exemption increase warrant article for the November 17th special town meeting, with research to be discussed at the September 23rd meeting.
Going forward, updating the town website's "how to read your vision card" guide will be the ongoing responsibility of whoever holds the lead/principal assessor position, rather than a board member.
The board set its next meeting dates as September 23rd, October 14th, and October 28th, replacing the originally planned October 7th and 21st dates due to scheduling conflicts.

what_happened.line: The board will not release the lien on a Chapter Land property until the town actually receives the owner's back-tax payment.
The town will not pursue rollback taxes on that property, instead collecting only the back taxes now owed on what has become three or four separate parcels.
The board agreed to seek a placeholder warrant article raising the veterans' property tax exemption for the November 17th special town meeting.
Review of August's already-processed excise tax abatements was pushed to the next meeting rather than taken up tonight.
The board reset its fall meeting schedule to September 23rd, October 14th, and October 28th.

why_it_matters: A property tax lien stays in force as leverage until back taxes are paid, and the town is not pursuing the larger rollback-tax penalty it could have sought on this Chapter Land property.
A veterans' exemption increase would go before voters as a warrant article at the November 17th special town meeting, and any increase is funded entirely by the town with no state reimbursement.
Routine items -- excise abatements, new-growth estimates, senior exemption applications -- remain in process rather than finalized this meeting.
